source.title: Stochastic normalized gradient descent with momentum for large-batch training
source.authors: Shen-Yi Zhao; Chang-Wei Shi; Yin-Peng Xie; Wu-Jun Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size effects on held-out performance with natural-label tasks and compares a normalized-gradient optimizer against standard momentum SGD and other large-batch methods.
record.gate_note: Reports test accuracy or perplexity across batch sizes, with training epochs stated for the experimental tasks. The convergence bounds are theoretical and do not measure test error, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out performance across batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets, testing V5 with momentum SGD and several alternative optimizers. Its optimizer comparisons also test whether changing the recipe reduces the large-batch penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors claim that their convergence bounds permit larger batches for SNGM than MSGD at the same gradient-computation budget, and that SNGM generally improves held-out performance over the tested large-batch baselines. They do not demonstrate that SNGM universally eliminates the penalty relative to its own small-batch performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares standard momentum SGD and other methods with SNGM, a normalized-gradient momentum update. Several experimental recipes use fixed epoch counts; ImageNet uses warm-up, while other image experiments omit warm-up. The experiments assess test accuracy or perplexity, not the training-to-test error gap directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with optimizer, batch size, dataset and model/task; ResNet20/CIFAR-10 uses no warm-up, while ImageNet uses warm-up and a polynomial learning-rate strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: DeepFM/Criteo, 10 epochs: increasing batch size from 1024 to 8192 reduces test AUC for MSGD, Adam, LARS and LAMB, while SNGM increases from 0.7489 to 0.7514.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch penalties and their dependence on optimizer extend to click-through-rate prediction.

fits_no_version.finding: The convergence analysis compares stationarity bounds and feasible batch sizes for MSGD, SNGM and block-wise updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient normalization can improve theoretical optimization guarantees for large-batch training under stated smoothness assumptions.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated test results. The experiments compare test performance by batch size but do not directly report the training-to-test error gap. The number of runs or seeds is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining rows for CIFAR-100 ViT and Wikitext-2 batch-size comparisons, plus the Criteo batch-size and optimizer comparisons, were omitted to stay within 60 rows. They appear in Tables 5, 6 and 8; the Criteo and Wikitext-2 results use different measures or settings than the image-classification claim version. Table 5 CIFAR-100 rows beyond R50 were also omitted due to the cap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization on image or language benchmarks under limited or broader tuning; switching optimizers and decoupled weight decay. Adam comparisons here concern CTR prediction.

Longer-training interventions, isolated learning-rate scaling or warm-up effects, and normalization or regularization interventions. ImageNet uses warm-up but provides no no-warm-up control. Only discrete batch sizes are sampled.
Dropout interventions; the LSTM uses a fixed dropout setting.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparison with norm or margin measures.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: The study's own introductory two-convolutional-layer CIFAR-10 experiment reports lower test accuracy and higher training loss with large-batch MSGD. No row or rows_left_out entry covers it; recover the figure's batch sizes, values and training budget before treating it as another fixed-epoch comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All tabulated values match the supplied text. Throughout the record, optimizer names occupy subject fields and should be paired with the actual model rather than classified as models themselves. All ViT rows use the base model identified in footnote 5. Wikitext-2 directly bears on V5 because V5 includes language models; its exclusion rationale is incorrect, although its omitted rows are declared. Declared omissions are evaluated from the supplied tables and are not duplicated in missing. No uncertainty or seed counts establish significance or equivalence for tiny differences. Numerical improvements at intermediate batches do not challenge V5's workload-dependent threshold or its explicit allowance for adapted recipes.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons on image-classification and language benchmarks under limited versus broader tuning; switching or decoupled weight decay.
No workload-dependent batch-size threshold is identified. No comparison tests longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, or batch-size matching at a fixed epoch budget for image classifiers.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.
